description: Capability-only reference entries for the six Blacklight Continuum Archetypes. These records explain what each Archetype can do, how its Resource and Pressure operate, and which power families it develops.

entries.title: Blacklight Basic Character Sheet
entries.summary: A browser-editable, autosaving, printable character sheet organized around identity, competence, powers, limitations, equipment, relationships, conditions, and advancement.
body: The Basic sheet records the character's present identity, nine Attributes, twenty-four Skills, Operational Frame, Archetype, derived traits, Resource, Pressure, innate abilities, ranked powers, equipment, relationships, limitations, conditions, and advancement.

The sheet follows a strict capability rule: appearance, species, physiology, substrate, origin, and descriptive transformation do not grant mechanics. A benefit exists only when recorded as an Attribute, Skill, specialization, innate ability, power, Operational Frame feature, equipment tag, condition, or explicit narrative permission.
Selecting an Archetype loads its Resource, Pressure, weakness, innate abilities, six power families, and thirty ranked powers. The sheet records present capabilities, costs, limits, and advancement.
The sheet supports browser autosave, JSON import and export, clearing, and print-to-PDF output.

tables.title: Derived Traits
rows: Archetype Base + Archetype Rating + Key Attribute

entries.title: Basic Archetypes
entries.summary: Six exceptional capability frameworks sharing one d10 chassis.
body: An Archetype defines the exceptional capabilities a character can develop, the Resource used to activate or intensify those capabilities, the Pressure that threatens control, the weakness that creates meaningful limits, and the power families available for advancement.

Archetype is not species, anatomy, biography, or profession. Operational Frame defines professional training. Archetype defines exceptional capability. Any Archetype can serve in any Operational Frame when the character's Skills support it.

Each Archetype contains six families with five ranked powers each. Power text defines activation, cost, test, effect, resistance, duration, and failure. Descriptive presentation never replaces those rules.

tables.title: Archetype Summary
rows: Evidence, discipline, identity defense, institutions, contingency, and human networks
Speed, command, concealment, resilience, feeding, and blood memory
Forms, pursuit, pack bonds, adaptation, spirits, and territory
Seals, manifestations, obligations, cognition, thresholds, and invocation
Projection, echoes, structures, emotion, phase, and memory
Networks, constructs, identity, machine relations, signals, and fabrication

entries.title: Human Investigator
entries.summary: A mortal specialist who competes with impossible threats through evidence, training, preparation, institutional literacy, relationships, and accountable judgment.
body: Conviction is the Investigator's Resource. It fuels decisive resistance, prepared solutions, protective action, institutional leverage, and the refusal to surrender a chosen principle.
Strain is the Investigator's Pressure. It accumulates through exhaustion, fear, isolation, overextension, unresolved responsibility, and repeated reliance on willpower beyond ordinary limits.

Casecraft establishes usable evidence and reconstructs responsibility. Field Discipline preserves action under danger. Continuity Anchoring protects identity and consent. Institutional Ghostcraft manipulates procedure and authority. Contingency Engineering preserves options. Human Network creates durable support through trust and organization.

tables.title: Six Power Families
rows: Tactical movement, protection, timing, and mortal defiance
Identity defense, shared baselines, and resistance to editing
Credentials, hierarchy, jurisdiction, and organization building
Tools, routes, caches, reversals, and failure analysis
Trust, witnesses, competent cells, obligations, and community

entries.title: Vampire
entries.summary: A Vitae-fueled predator whose powers govern supernatural speed, authority, concealment, resilience, feeding, and inherited memory.
body: Vitae is the Vampire's Resource. It fuels physical acceleration, supernatural command, concealment, recovery, predation, and lineage effects.
Hunger is the Vampire's Pressure. It increases when Vitae is depleted, feeding is delayed, predatory compulsion is denied, or powers demand more than the character can safely provide.

Crimson Velocity controls speed and action economy. Grave Dominion controls predatory authority. Veil of Night controls recognition and concealment. Deathless Resilience controls survival and recovery. Vital Predation controls feeding and function theft. Blood Memory controls inherited information, stored experience, and lineage creation.

tables.title: Six Power Families
rows: Speed, reactions, additional motion, and temporal advantage
Command, fixation, group presence, and predatory authority
Stealth, altered recognition, disguise, and memory concealment
Healing, dormancy, armor, catastrophic survival, and persistence
Feeding analysis, unfamiliar sources, hunting, and function theft
Memory extraction, sharing, inherited skill, ancestors, and lineage creation

entries.title: Shapechanger
entries.summary: A supernatural transformer whose powers govern forms, pursuit, pack continuity, adaptive capabilities, spirit relations, and territorial sovereignty.
body: Fury is the Shapechanger's Resource. It fuels rapid transformation, pursuit, protection, environmental adaptation, spirit action, and territorial control.
Instinct is the Shapechanger's Pressure. It rises through denied pursuit, threatened packmates, violated territory, humiliation, confinement, and extended use of predatory forms.

Threefold Form supplies the basic permission to shift among social, hunting, and war forms. Warform defines combat benefits. Hunt Across Worlds defines pursuit. Pack Continuity defines bonded coordination. Adaptive Forms defines utility transformations. Spirit Ecology defines spirit interaction. Territorial Sovereignty defines claimed domains.

tables.title: Six Power Families
rows: Combat transformation, weapons, scale, defenses, and apex shape
Tracking through disguise, transfer, systems, and altered identity
Bond sensing, coordination, shared harm, and collective defense
Utility traits, borrowed functions, environments, and stable new forms
Detection, thresholds, pacts, reflection travel, and new totems
Claims, warnings, perimeter awareness, environmental defense, and domains

entries.title: Eldritch Binder
entries.summary: A negotiator, jailer, host, or partner whose capabilities arise from a structured relationship with an impossible presence.
body: Pact is the Binder's Resource. It represents usable authority, negotiated permission, stored obligation, and controlled access to the answering presence.
Intrusion is the Binder's Pressure. It measures attention, influence, knowledge, access, and leverage gained by the presence through repeated use.

Sealcraft controls boundaries and local law. Borrowed Manifestation grants temporary capabilities. Pact Economy governs prices and obligations. Forbidden Cognition grants dangerous knowledge. Threshold Geometry creates nonordinary routes. Invocation controls signs, avatars, partial arrivals, and full audiences.

tables.title: Six Power Families
rows: Boundaries, prohibitions, anchoring, prisons, and local law
Senses, reach, defenses, movement, and hybrid states
Prices, deferred costs, obligation transfer, renegotiation, and contracts
Anomaly reading, translation, patron questions, unrealized memory, and dangerous knowledge
Folded reach, impossible angles, doors, transit, and persistent routes
Signs, channels, avatars, partial arrival, and negotiated audience

entries.title: Harmonic Mutant
entries.summary: A resonance wielder whose powers affect force, patterns, structures, emotion, phase, and memory through a chosen harmonic medium.
body: Resonance is the Mutant's Resource. It fuels projection, healing, structural interaction, emotional modulation, phase effects, and memory work.

Discord is the Mutant's Pressure. It accumulates through incompatible frequencies, emotional shock, repeated projection, environmental coupling, unstable phase effects, and uncontrolled sympathetic response.

Harmonic Projection controls force. Echo Patterns controls healing and duplication. Structural Resonance controls architecture and machinery. Emotional Chord controls collective state. Phase Modulation controls interaction with matter and nearby outcomes. Memory Harmonics controls recovery, storage, separation, and preservation of memory patterns.

tables.title: Six Power Families
rows: Force, disruption, shielding, catastrophic chords, and area effects
Healing, doubles, links, lasting alterations, and chorus selves
Sensing, stress control, bracing, activation, and system integration
Mood sensing, panic control, crowd tuning, bonds, and shared intent
Friction, passage, interleaving, causal evasion, and between-state existence
Recall, imprinting, recovery, perspective splitting, and preserved identity messages

entries.title: Technomancer
entries.summary: A network and fabrication specialist whose powers govern system authority, constructs, noospheric identity, machine relationships, signal warfare, and advanced production.
body: Bandwidth is the Technomancer's Resource. It measures usable attention, active connections, processing, permissions, and interface capacity committed to current effects.

Feedback is the Technomancer's Pressure. It accumulates through hostile access, reciprocal surveillance, synchronization, identity contamination, overloaded channels, and autonomous systems acting back through the connection.

Network Dominion controls access and authority. Construct Engineering creates tools and systems. Noospheric Identity controls recognized personhood. Machine Communion governs relationships with autonomous intelligences. Signal Warfare controls connectivity and denial. Fabrication Interface governs template reading, repairs, production, and complex creation.

tables.title: Six Power Families
rows: Commands, unauthorized access, possession, distribution, and local control
Tools, helper processes, barriers, swarms, and emergency devices
Credentials, provisional personhood, borrowed roles, ownership, and rooted identities
System needs, negotiation, awakening, partnership, and machine assemblies
Jamming, defense, quarantine, targeted hostile signals, and blackouts
Template reading, repairs, peripherals, rule alteration, and complex creation
